text:
Riley (oncall): FYI — started getting customer p99 latency alerts right after the 03:00 UTC deploy. Several Dedicated customers reporting 10-30s tail latency. looks like scale-up/attach lag + cold GPU starts.
Mia Chen: seeing same in eu-west1 and us-west2. p95 jumped from ~350ms -> 1.2s, p99 up to ~18s for some requests.
Samir Patel: logs show a spike in attach_pending and image_pull for dedicated pools at 03:02. attach retries stacking.
Jordan K: can confirm. stacktrace from router: 
```
2026-03-15T03:02:11Z WARN attach: attach_pending=612 attach_wait_ms=18000 pool=d-ed-42 region=eu-west1
2026-03-15T03:02:12Z ERROR kube: image_pull_timeout backlog=120
```
Samir Patel: also saw 401 bursts for a handful of token-auth customers around same time — might be auth retries increasing load.
Lee Ortega: is this only Dedicated? Hosted doesn't show same P99 jump. implies provisioning path issue.
opsbot: Alert: dedicated-pool-attach-rate high (600/s) — autoscale backlog rising — cluster-provisioner queue length 8k.
Riley (oncall): immediate ask: can we triage and apply a quick mitigation to reduce customer impact? priority customers flagged.
Mia Chen: quick mitigations I suggest:
- temporarily route flagged customers to hosted fallback (if tenant allows)
- bump min_pool_size for vulnerable dedicated pools to keep spare warm GPUs
- increase attach retry_backoff jitter to reduce thundering herd
- pre-pull image for current runtime version across pool nodes
Samir Patel: I'm doing a manual reserve of 4 GPUs in eu-west1 for the affected pools now (holding 4 warm nodes) — will update once done.
Jordan K: I'll push a hotfix to attacher to extend image_pull timeout and log extra context (small change, can roll to 2 regions quickly).
Lee Ortega: I'll open a short-term canary rollback to previous deploy for the control plane path that touched node provisioning. if rollback confirms regression we can revert deploy.
Support Bot: Confirmed 3 high-priority customer escalations opened at 03:05. CS alerted and offered hosted fallback.
Riley (oncall): repro steps for infra folks:
1) curl reproduce (small request) against dedicated route, sample: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.test/v1/dedicated/run?model=gpt-small
```
2) watch attach_pending metric: kubectl logs provisioner | grep attach_pending
3) look for image_pull_timeout and attach_retry metrics in graphite/observability
Samir Patel: mitigation timeline:
- +2m manual warm reserve applied in eu-west1 (done)
- +6m increase attacher timeout and roll to us-west2 (in flight)
- +12m route 2 flagged customers to hosted fallback (requires CS opt-in)
Riley (oncall): post-mitigation checks: confirm p99 drops back under SLA (target <2s) and attach queue drains.
Mia Chen: quick numbers after warm reserve (eu-west1): p95 -> 420ms, p99 -> 2.6s (improved but still elevated). attach_queue dropped from 7k -> 900.
Jordan K: rolled attach timeout patch to us-west2, image_pull timeouts reduced, attach failures down ~70%.
Lee Ortega: started controlled rollback of control plane bits to pre-deploy commit just now. monitoring for regressions.
Riley (oncall): longer-term follow-ups (create tickets):
- Add prewarm job to proactively keep a small warm buffer during deploy windows
- Improve fairshare logic to avoid punishing smaller customers during global attach spikes
- Add adaptive backoff to attach retries with token-aware jitter
- Add synthetic test in deploy pipeline to simulate attach storm and fail deploy if provisioning latency > threshold
Samir Patel: logging action: add a metric for consecutive auth 401 bursts tied to attach rate so we can correlate auth churn -> attach storms.
Support Bot: customers updated with workaround and ETA for fix, flagged for follow-up post-mitigation.
Riley (oncall): thanks all. we're keeping this thread as the incident notes. if rollback proves clear fix we'll lock the change and follow up with postmortem. :thumbsup:
